reviewer_mode: independent hostile AAA scapular-counterforce and pre-engine gate

scope.judged_unit: Scapular Counterforce Lock — upper-body force arrest
scope.isolated_question: Whether the strongest Round012 keyframe creates an unmistakable high-forward leading shoulder and low-back trailing shoulder, acute folded leading elbow, down-left trailing-elbow return triangle, deep ribcage-pelvis counterrotation, and one violent arrested stop while preserving identity, same-hilt contact, blade mass, and the frozen lower load.
claims_not_made: 3D, rig, mesh, UV, deformation, collision, animation, LOD, engine, game-ready, or production-ready status
legal originality, exclusivity, copyright clearance, or trademark clearance

attempts.fresh_finding: The shoulder order is reversed, the trailing contact collapses near the guard, and the unequal-elbow chain is unreadable.
Both contacts separate clearly, but the viewer-left trailing shoulder stays high at the jaw and both arms remain a paired reach.
The grip is clean, yet the high trailing shoulder, similar elbow extension, and nearly upright torso make this the clearest hauling failure.

The strongest attempt finally puts the viewer-right leading shoulder above a jaw-cleared viewer-left trailing shoulder and preserves complete separated contacts, but both elbows stay long and no return triangle or violent counterforce lock appears.

checks.contract: leading shoulder high-forward and trailing shoulder back-low
checks.finding: Candidate 04 is the first attempt with the correct viewer-right-high/viewer-left-low order and a pale jaw-to-shoulder gap, but the height delta remains modest rather than one emphatic shoulder-cap step.

checks.contract: leading elbow short and acutely folded
checks.finding: The weapon-side arm reaches long toward the guard; no acute elbow fold nests beneath the high leading shoulder.

checks.contract: trailing elbow far down-left with forearm returning to grip
checks.finding: The trailing arm runs almost straight from shoulder to hand instead of dropping to an external low elbow and returning up-right.

checks.contract: large triangular negative space around trailing arm
checks.finding: Because the trailing arm lacks a bent return path, the required pale triangle between torso, upper arm, and forearm does not exist.

checks.contract: deep loaded C-curve and ribcage-pelvis counterrotation
checks.finding: The torso leans and turns slightly, but the spine remains long and the ribcage does not visibly side-bend and torque against the frozen pelvis.

checks.contract: complete widely separated contacts on one continuous hilt
checks.finding: Both complete hands visibly close around widely separated regions of one continuous cobalt hilt with a conspicuous exposed wrap span.
The huge planted right load column, airborne rear heel, toe-only skid, and small gouge remain readable, although the front boot remains overinflated.

checks.contract: one violent arrested stop rather than paired hauling
checks.finding: The two long arms pull opposite ends of the hilt like a bar; the blade mass does not resolve through unequal elbows, scapulae, ribs, and pelvis as one stop.

identity_and_design_continuity.finding: The mature face, palette, capacitor, copper routing, asymmetrical greaves, and broad storm-shear remain recognizable, but the chest harness/yoke, shoulder armor, hair response, and some hilt attachment details drift; the hair again reads as two opposed tail forms.

private_benchmark_comparison.method: Six relevant private gameplay views were reviewed as sequential unlabeled A/B pairs with independently randomized candidate/reference order. Original aspect ratios were preserved, no retouching was performed, and no comparison composite was created. Temporary private extraction was deleted after inspection and no private pixels were copied into the repository or publication.

comparisons.focus: shoulder-height delta, scapular order, and action commitment
comparisons.finding: The candidate corrects shoulder order, but its modest delta and quiet clavicle line do not approach the benchmark's forceful whole-torso commitment.

comparisons.focus: leading folded elbow and weapon-load compression
comparisons.finding: The benchmark compresses shoulder, elbow, and ribcage beneath the weapon path; the candidate's leading arm remains long and uncompressed.

comparisons.focus: trailing-elbow return path and negative-space authorship
comparisons.finding: The benchmark creates readable arm overlap and directional load around a committed action arc; the candidate supplies no external down-left elbow return or triangular counterforce space.

comparisons.focus: complete hand contact and separated grip readability
comparisons.finding: The candidate's two complete hands, visible digits, broad separation, continuous hilt ingress/egress, and exposed wrap are exceptionally clear in the isolated frame.

comparisons.focus: deep C-curve, counterrotation, and anatomical torsion
comparisons.finding: The benchmark carries contact through shoulder, chest, waist, and stance; the candidate's ribs and pelvis remain too aligned and its spine too long for comparable torsion.

comparisons.focus: lower-load resolution and one violent stop
comparisons.finding: The candidate preserves a stronger isolated foot silhouette, but it lacks the benchmark's phase-specific recoil, impact context, and linked upper-to-lower-body force resolution.

scorecard.scale: 0-10 per category; ten categories sum directly to 100

categories.finding: Nyra remains recognizable, but doubled hair motion and drift in harness, yoke, shoulder armor, and hilt attachments break a strict freeze.
Candidate 04 finally establishes the correct high-right/low-left order and jaw gap, yet the height split and scapular displacement are too modest for a lock.
The leading elbow is not acutely flexed beneath the shoulder; the whole arm reaches long toward the guard.

categories.category: trailing elbow return and triangular negative space
categories.finding: The trailing elbow never drops outside and below the torso, the forearm never returns up-right, and the required triangle is absent.
There is slight lean and turn, but no deep loaded side-bend or forceful ribcage opposition against the pelvis.
Both complete hands are widely separated, readable, and convincingly wrapped around one continuous exposed hilt.
The dominant planted right leg and airborne toe-skid rear contact survive, though the front boot's block inflation remains implausible.
The full silhouette reads cleanly, but the long bilateral arms, quiet torso, huge boot, and extreme blade-to-hilt leverage remain mechanically weak.
The studio illustration is polished and material classes separate clearly, but uniform presentation and repeated micro-detail remain below authored gameplay response.
Bounded provenance is documented and non-derivative, but the candidate meets only 1 of 6 private comparisons and reads as paired hauling rather than a phase-specific stop.

engine_and_game_capture_truth.finding: The workspace contains an installed editor and a Unity template/review shell, but no Nyra Round012 integration, runtime gameplay controller, encounter scene, or player build. Running unrelated review content could not produce matched gameplay evidence for this 2D proof, so no engine run or fabricated capture was performed.

paid3D.finding: Paid 3D remains denied and unused because the isolated target, composite score, category floor, and five-of-six benchmark gates all fail.

single_biggest_remaining_gap: The unequal-elbow counterforce topology is absent: the leading elbow stays long instead of folding while the trailing arm never drops down-left and returns, so no triangular push-pull mechanism appears and the pose reads as paired hauling.
round013_prescription_limited_to_single_: Freeze every other judged fact; re-author only the elbow and forearm paths by folding the leading elbow acutely beneath its existing high shoulder and placing the trailing elbow far down-left below the hilt before returning that forearm to its existing grip, leaving the required pale triangle open.
